deed: ארגון הסיוע הישראלי איסראייד מספק תמיכה נפשית ומים נקיים לפליטי אוקראינה
title: IsraAID helps Ukraine's refugees with psychological support and clean water

trailer.text: The aid organization IsraAID, which the Jerusalem Post describes as a global organization based in Israel that helps distressed people worldwide, has worked, according to the newspaper, in 56 countries for over two decades.
According to the organization, when the Russian invasion began in February 2022 it arrived in Moldova and within days set up essential services at the border for fleeing refugees.
In June 2022 the organization expanded its operations into Ukraine.
According to Michal Bar, its director of emergency programs, it provided the city of Mykolaiv with four reverse osmosis machines for drinking water.
According to a report by the organization from January 2026, a network of more than 100 trained psychologists provides mental health support in hospitals across Ukraine.

glance.label: Scope
glance.value: More than 330,000 people (according to the organization, February 2023)

glance.label: Water
glance.value: More than 600,000 liters free of charge in Mykolaiv (according to the organization)

stations.title: Before: the decision to set out

paragraphs.text: According to Israel21c in August 2022, in the six months since the invasion some 5,000 Ukrainian civilians had been killed and 12.5 million displaced.
Michal Bar, IsraAID's director of emergency programs and operations, said that they were seeing the highest number of refugees since the Second World War.
According to JNS, the organization's aid workers are used to disasters, but they admit that what is happening in Ukraine is exceptional.
Yotam Polizer, the CEO of IsraAID, is described in the Jerusalem Post as 38 years old.
He said that at first the organization said it had to respond, but not send teams to an active war zone.
According to Polizer, on Saturday, February 26, 2022, an IsraAID team left Israel.

He explained that Moldova was chosen, among other reasons, because, compared to the other countries that took in refugees, it is the only neighboring country that is not a member of the European Union or NATO.

stations.title: A tent for mothers and children on the Moldovan border

paragraphs.text: According to the organization, essential services for fleeing refugees were set up at the border within days.
According to PhotoIsrael, the first task was setting up a safe space for mothers and children.
According to Polizer, IsraAID's tent at the border was a safe space where mothers rested and children played.
He said that the children's spaces held kindergarten-like activities: play, learning and stress relief for the children, and rest for the mothers.
Polizer also said that the organization distributed thermal blankets to thousands of refugees.
According to Polizer, the organization recruited a large number of Russian-speaking Israelis with experience in social work and psychology.
According to him, about 35 IsraAID staff were then working on the ground in Moldova.
According to IsraAID, in its first three months in Moldova the organization served 4,000 people directly, at the border and in shelters across the country.
According to the organization, in May 2022 some 670 children and mothers were still attending its mental health activities each week.

stations.title: A logistics hub in Tulcea, Romania

paragraphs.text: According to IsraAID, in March 2022 the organization opened a humanitarian logistics hub in Tulcea, Romania.
It worked there with local and international partners and with Ukrainian volunteers.
According to the organization, the hub used technology from the Israeli company Monday.com to track aid deliveries without GPS.
According to IsraAID, the organization also set up a logistics hub in Odesa.
The aim was to strengthen the supply chain from the Tulcea hub to cities in Ukraine.

According to the organization, with the opening of the humanitarian logistics hub in Tulcea, Romania, in March 2022 and its supply chain to southern Ukraine, it expanded and reached more than 30 regions with more than 3,000 tons of essential items, including over 5.6 million food rations.

stations.title: Into Ukraine: learning to breathe in Bucha

paragraphs.text: According to IsraAID, after about four months on the borders of Moldova and Romania, the organization expanded its operations into Ukraine itself in June 2022.
According to eJewishPhilanthropy, the initiatives inside Ukraine grew out of a concern that Ukrainians inside the country were being left behind by aid efforts.
According to the same site, by July 2022 one IsraAID team was already operating in Odesa.
According to IsraAID, in June 2022 psychologists and social workers in Irpin and Bucha were trained in mental health and psychosocial support.
During a visit to Bucha in July 2022, Ukrainian social workers and soldiers gathered.
They learned breathing and physical exercises from an IsraAID expert to reduce post-traumatic stress.
Polizer said that many of the participants said it was the first time they had been able to breathe and relieve their stress.
According to eJewishPhilanthropy, the organization gained its expertise in trauma counseling using methods developed in Israeli cities such as Sderot and Kiryat Shmona.
Ukraine's First Lady, Olena Zelenska, made access to mental health care a national priority.
Polizer was surprised that the Ukrainian government was giving priority to trauma care.
According to eJewishPhilanthropy in July 2022, IsraAID would send teams of Israeli trauma specialists to Ukraine for several weeks at a time.
According to the same report, the organization would also station 10 to 15 aid workers there full-time.
Polizer estimated at the time that the new efforts would require more than $10 million in additional funds from the organization.
Pavlo Didnyk, IsraAID's water engineer in Ukraine, said that Mykolaiv had no water supply whatsoever for more than a month.
According to eJewishPhilanthropy, the organization worked with municipal officials to bring industrial water filtration systems to the city.
According to the same site, the organization hired a local water engineer.
According to Michal Bar, IsraAID worked with the municipality on locating groundwater.
According to her, the organization provided the city with four reverse osmosis machines for drinking water.
In this work the organization partnered with MASHAV and the Israeli Embassy in Ukraine.
According to IsraAID in February 2023, the reverse osmosis stations in Mykolaiv had processed more than 600,000 liters of water and dispensed them free of charge to the city's residents.
According to a report by the organization from January 2026, it has to date installed more than 100 water supply and treatment units and rehabilitated dozens of boreholes.
Jewish Press describes IsraAID as the Israeli non-governmental humanitarian aid organization that is helping Ukraine build a mental health infrastructure.
According to the newspaper, the initiative includes funding and training psychologists, social workers and other mental health providers.
They will be deployed to hospitals in Ukrainian cities.
According to IsraAID, in September 2022 the organization recruited and trained 60 psychologists and placed them in hospitals in Kyiv, Dnipro and Vinnytsia.
According to the organization, its protection specialists also trained key staff at the Ministry of Health in dealing with burnout, self-care and Psychological First Aid.

According to IsraAID, in January 2023 the organization's psychologists in hospitals in the Dnipro and Kyiv regions provided urgent, free psychological support to families of casualties and to first responders.
According to the organization, at the time of the attack on April 17, 2025, psychologists it had trained were already in hospitals across the country.
In the fourth cohort of the Doctor, Psychologist, Patient program, 30 more clinical psychologists began advanced training, according to the organization.
According to a report from January 2026, a network of more than 100 trained psychologists provides mental health support in hospitals across Ukraine.
According to IsraAID, when Kherson was liberated in November 2022, the organization was among the first to arrive there.
It brought over $2 million of medical supplies for the three hospitals.
According to the organization, in December 2022 it distributed blankets, generators and thermal clothing, keeping more than 17,500 vulnerable people warm.
According to IsraAID in February 2023, through mobile clinics and distribution of medicines to hospitals, it had reached more than 40,000 people with medical support.
That same month the organization reported that its teams in Ukraine, Moldova and Romania had reached more than 330,000 people.
They did so together with a network of more than 100 partners.
According to JNS in August 2022, IsraAID announced a five-year plan to expand its programs in Ukraine.
Polizer said that an average project of the organization lasts five to seven years in the same place.
According to IsraAID in September 2025, the organization had trained nearly 300 staff members from 17 schools.
According to the same report, 31 educational institutions are participating in the program.
In January 2026 the organization reported that it had completed a major initiative training 760 railway workers across nine provinces in life-saving first aid.
According to Polizer, in the first five months of the invasion IsraAID received more support from Israelis than at any time in the organization's history.
He told the Jerusalem Post that for the Ukraine crisis the organization received over a million dollars from Israeli donors.
According to him, this is about as much as in all of the previous 20 years combined.

disagreements.question: How many refugees crossed into Moldova?

versions.says: Israel21c (August 2022): some 560,000 Ukrainians, mainly women and children, fled to Moldova at the start of the war, and some 100,000 remained there
Yotam Polizer: more than 400,000 people crossed into Moldova

disagreements.question: How many centers for women and children operated in Moldova?

versions.says: Israel21c (August 2022): IsraAID and local partners run five community centers with daycare, psychosocial support and resilience-building activities
Yotam Polizer (around May 2022): the organization had set up seven centers for women and children that were still operating

disagreements.question: What was the value of the aid delivered?

versions.says: Israel21c (August 2022): about $30 million worth of food and medical and hygiene supplies had been shipped through the Tulcea hub by then
According to Jewish Press (September 2022), IsraAID had by then delivered, together with international partners, essential aid worth more than $35 million.

disagreements.question: How many years has the humanitarian work been going on?

versions.says: Polizer to eJewishPhilanthropy: he has been doing this work for 15 years
Polizer to the Jerusalem Post: he has been doing this work for 14 years

disagreements.question: How many Ukrainians need humanitarian assistance?

versions.says: JNS (August 2022): IsraAID estimated that 16 million Ukrainians need assistance
IsraAID (February 2023): 17.7 million Ukrainians still needed assistance

disagreements.question: When did IsraAID begin training care professionals in Bucha?

versions.says: IsraAID (one-year-of-war timeline): In June 2022, upon entering Ukraine, psychologists and social workers were trained in Irpin and Bucha
eJewishPhilanthropy (July 2022): In early June the organization had only approached the Ukrainian government. The first session in Bucha was an unplanned pilot during Polizer's visit in early July

claims.text: לפי IsraAID, בהתקפה ב-17 באפריל 2025 פסיכולוגים שהוכשרו על ידה כבר היו בבתי חולים ברחבי המדינה ותמכו בחולים, במשפחות וברופאים.
claims.quote: IsraAID-trained psychologists were already embedded in hospitals across the country and ready to offer immediate support to patients, families, and doctors.

claims.text: לפי IsraAID, במחזור רביעי של התוכנית "רופא, פסיכולוג, מטופל" החלו 30 פסיכולוגים קליניים נוספים בהכשרה מתקדמת.
claims.quote: with 30 more clinical psychologists starting advanced training to deliver practical psychosocial care in hospitals

claims.text: לפי IsraAID, כשחרסון שוחררה בנובמבר 2022 הארגון היה בין הראשונים שהגיעו אליה עם ציוד רפואי בשווי מעל 2 מיליון דולר לשלושת בתי החולים.
claims.quote: IsraAID is among the first to arrive with over $2 million of medical supplies for the city’s three hospitals.

claims.text: לפי IsraAID, בדצמבר 2022 היא חילקה שמיכות, גנרטורים ולבוש תרמי ושמרה על חום ליותר מ-17,500 אנשים פגיעים.
claims.quote: IsraAID distributes blankets, generators, and thermal clothing - keeping over 17,500 vulnerable elderly people, children, and others warm.

claims.text: לפי IsraAID (פברואר 2023), באמצעות מרפאות ניידות וחלוקת תרופות לבתי חולים הגיעה לתמיכה רפואית ליותר מ-40,000 איש.
claims.quote: we have reached more than 40,000 people with medical support

claims.text: לפי JNS באוגוסט 2022, IsraAID העריכה ש-16 מיליון אוקראינים נזקקים לסיוע הומניטרי והודיעה על תוכנית חמש שנים להרחבת תוכניות שם.
claims.quote: Estimating that 16 million Ukrainians are now in desperate need of humanitarian assistance, IsraAID has announced a five-year plan to continue and expand multiple programs there.

claims.text: פוליצר אמר שפרויקט ממוצע של IsraAID נמשך חמש עד שבע שנים באותו מקום.
claims.quote: For us an average project is five to seven years in a place.

claims.text: לפי IsraAID בספטמבר 2025, הארגון הכשיר כמעט 300 אנשי צוות מ-17 בתי ספר, ו-31 מוסדות חינוך משתתפים בתוכנית.
claims.quote: We've already trained nearly 300 staff members from 17 schools, with 31 educational institutions now participating in the program.

claims.text: לפי IsraAID בינואר 2026, הארגון סיים יוזמה גדולה להכשרת 760 עובדי רכבת בתשעה מחוזות בעזרה ראשונה מצילת חיים.
claims.quote: we recently completed a major initiative training 760 railway workers across nine provinces in life-saving first aid.

claims.text: לפי פוליצר, ב-5 החודשים הראשונים של הפלישה IsraAID קיבלה מישראלים תמיכה רבה יותר מאי פעם בהיסטוריה של הארגון.
claims.quote: IsraAid has received more support from Israelis over the past five months than at any previous time in the history of the organization

claims.text: פוליצר אמר לג'רוזלם פוסט שבמשבר אוקראינה IsraAID קיבלה מתורמים ישראלים יותר ממיליון דולר, בערך כמו בכל 20 השנים הקודמות יחד.
claims.quote: we received over a million dollars from Israeli donors for this crisis specifically, which is more or less what we received from Israeli donors in the last 20 years combined

claims.text: לפי Israel21c באוגוסט 2022, כ-560,000 אוקראינים, בעיקר נשים וילדים, נמלטו למולדובה בתחילת המלחמה וכ-100,000 נותרו שם.
claims.quote: Some 560,000 Ukrainians, mainly women and children, fled to Moldova at the start of the war.

claims.text: פוליצר אמר שיותר מ-400,000 איש חצו למולדובה.
claims.quote: More than 400,000 people have crossed through to Moldova, and some are continuing to Western Europe, but many are staying.

claims.text: לפי Israel21c באוגוסט 2022, IsraAID ושותפים מקומיים מפעילים במולדובה חמישה מרכזי קהילה עם מעון יום, תמיכה פסיכו-סוציאלית ופעילויות לבניית חוסן.
claims.quote: IsraAID and local partners run five community centers in Moldova providing daycare, psychosocial support, recreation and resilience-building activities.

claims.text: פוליצר אמר (בערך במאי 2022) ש-IsraAID הקימה שבעה מרכזים לנשים וילדים שעדיין פועלים.
claims.quote: We've started seven of these centers for women and children so far that we're still operating.

claims.text: לפי Israel21c באוגוסט 2022, דרך מרכז לוגיסטי שהקימה IsraAID בטולצ'ה ברומניה נשלחו עד אז מזון וציוד רפואי והיגייני בשווי כ-30 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: IsraAID established a logistics hub in Tulcea, Romania, through which about $30 million worth of food and medical and hygiene supplies have so far been shipped

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press בספטמבר 2022, IsraAID העבירה עד אז סיוע חיוני בשווי של יותר מ-35 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: IsraAID has delivered over $35 million worth of essential aid

claims.text: לפי IsraAID בפברואר 2023, 17.7 מיליון אוקראינים עדיין נזקקו לסיוע הומניטרי.
claims.quote: as we mark one year of conflict, 17.7 million Ukrainians still need humanitarian support

claims.text: IsraAID (ציר הזמן לשנה למלחמה): ביוני 2022, עם הכניסה לאוקראינה, הוכשרו פסיכולוגים ועובדים סוציאליים באירפין ובבוצ'ה
claims.quote: mental health and psychosocial support training for psychologists and social workers in Irpin and Bucha
